name: Men's perms

card.summary: A chemical hair treatment that sets curls or waves into men's hair, adding volume and texture so styling is easier and the head shape and hairline look fuller.
card.aka: Perm for men, textured perm, wavy perm
card.note: Chemical treatment can damage hair if hair is already compromised or coloured.

quick.overview:
A perm uses chemicals to reshape hair's structure so it holds curls or waves. For men it adds volume, texture and a more styled outline, which can make thinner or flat hair look fuller and cut down daily styling.

The technique goes back to the early 1900s, and men's perms were common in the 1970s and 1980s. Stylists have described renewed interest among younger men in recent years, usually in softer, looser versions.
quick.how: A stylist applies a reducing lotion to hair wound around rods, then an oxidizing neutralizer to set the new shape. Modern perms use a pH of roughly 8 to 9.5 for 15 to 30 minutes of processing. Acid perms suit finer hair.
quick.risks: Perm chemistry can damage hair, particularly strongly alkaline formulations, and earlier methods caused burns. Gentler low-pH formulations keep the cuticle more closed. Coloured or already damaged hair is a common concern for stylists.

lead: A perm chemically reshapes hair so it holds curls or waves. Men use perms to add volume, texture and shape, which can make flat or thinning hair look fuller and make it easier to style. [1]
Modern perms work by breaking the disulfide bonds in hair keratin with a reducing lotion such as ammonium thioglycolate, then re-forming them with an oxidizing lotion around a rod. [1]
Men wore perms widely in the 1970s and 1980s, and stylists report a renewed trend among younger men in softer, textured versions.

chain: Hair is shaped on rods and neutralized
Lasting curls add volume and texture
angle.text: A perm gives a lasting curl or wave in the hair, adding volume and texture and reducing daily styling. It can help hair look thicker.

infobox: Ammonium or sodium thioglycolate, then peroxide neutralizer

paras: Marcel Grateau introduced a practical thermal waving method in 1872. Karl Nessler demonstrated an electric spiral heat perm on 8 October 1905, using caustic soda and about six hours of processing, which suited only long hair. [1]

Eugene Suter and Isidoro Calvete developed heaters and reagents from 1917. In 1931 Ralph Evans and Everett McDonough showed a heatless overnight method, and Arnold Willatt invented the cold wave in 1938, eliminating machines and heat. Home kits such as Toni popularized perming. [1]

Alkaline perms (pH about 9 to 10) suit coarse hair and work at room temperature; acid perms (pH about 6.5 to 8.2, using glyceryl monothioglycolate) suit fine hair, need added heat and keep the cuticle more closed. Digital perms were introduced in the 21st century. [1]
Early electric systems caused burns, and high-heat waving could degrade hair. Harsh alkaline recipes could not safely touch skin, and low-pH formulations are described as reducing damage. [1]
